rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This problem-solving plan starts with the meaning and steps of the product rule, using one complete example before a similar attempt. Four 15-minute sessions fit the available windows. Guidance then fades into retrieval, varied application, and an independent check.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build the product rule from the need to differentiate a product of two functions.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model and one complete worked example
contentTargets: Meaning and formula of the product rule: (fg)' = f'g + fg'
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating a product is not generally the same as multiplying the two derivatives.
Apply the formula to one problem that closely matches the worked example.

sessions.title: Carry Out the Procedure
sessions.objective: Use the product rule one visible step at a time with polynomial factors.
sessions.amountLabel: One polynomial-product example and one guided attempt
contentTargets: Identify f, g, f', and g', then substitute and simplify
completionEvidence: Construct a labeled product-rule setup for one polynomial product.
Solve the derivative and simplify the result.

sessions.title: Retrieve and Apply the Rule
sessions.objective: Recall the rule without a model and apply it to two differently presented products.
sessions.amountLabel: One recalled formula and two short applications
contentTargets: Product-rule retrieval and application when factors look different
completionEvidence: Recall the product-rule formula without prompts.
Solve two product-rule derivatives, repairing any setup error after feedback.

sessions.title: Independent Product-Rule Check
sessions.objective: Choose and use the product rule independently, then verify the result.
sessions.amountLabel: Two independent derivative problems with verification
contentTargets: Independent recognition, execution, and checking of product-rule problems
completionEvidence: Classify which of two derivative problems requires the product rule.
Solve the product-rule problem independently and explain each term in the result.

activities.title: Name the Product Rule
activities.body: Answer from memory, but keep the formula in view if needed. Then submit your response.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product fg is f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: A complete answer gives the derivative of a product as the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: Independent recall
activities.title: Choose the Rule Form
activities.body: Pick the formula that matches the product rule. Do not use the model.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product fg is f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: The product rule uses one derivative on each factor, but not on both at once and not on neither.

activities.label: Wrap up
activities.title: What the Rule Means
activities.body: Write one short takeaway from today. Keep it to one sentence.
activities.concept: The product rule says the derivative of a product fg is f'g + fg'.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is f'g + fg'
activities.feedback: A good takeaway names the two-part structure and avoids the common mistake of differentiating both factors in every term.
